t: LeetCode 2074 - Reverse Nodes in Even Length Groups: Groupwise Pointer Surgery
o: **Understanding the problem.** Consecutive nodes are dealt into groups sized 1, 2, 3, and so on; every group whose realized length is even must be reversed, and the trailing group may hold fewer nodes than its nominal size - its real length decides. In [5,2,6,3,9,1,7,3,8,4] the groups are [5], [2,6], [3,9,1], [7,3,8,4]; flipping the two even ones yields [5,6,2,3,9,1,4,8,3,7]. In [1,1,0,6,5] the last nominal group of size 3 contains only [6,5], whose length 2 is even, so it flips too, producing [1,0,1,5,6]. With up to 100000 nodes a single orderly pass - or a value-array rebuild - keeps everything linear.
k: Group parity is judged by the actual node count, which only differs from the nominal size for the final group.
After reversing a chunk, its former head becomes the chunk tail - the natural anchor for continuing.
An array round-trip sidesteps pointer surgery at the cost of O(n) auxiliary memory.

a.n: Approach 1: Rebuild From a Value Array
a.i: Flatten the values, re-chunk them following sizes 1, 2, 3, ... with each chunk capped by what remains, reversing even chunks, then relink. Correctness is immediate because grouping and reversal happen on plain data rather than live pointers.
s: Copy the list values into an array.
Consume chunks of size min(g, remaining) for g = 1, 2, 3, ....
Relink the reordered values into a fresh list.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def reverseEvenLengthGroups(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        vals = []
        node = head
        while node:
            vals.append(node.val)
            node = node.next
        n = len(vals)
        res = []
        i = 0
        g = 1
        while i < n:
            length = min(g, n - i)
            chunk = vals[i:i + length]
            if length % 2 == 0:
                chunk.reverse()
            res.extend(chunk)
            i += length
            g += 1
        dummy = ListNode(0)
        cur = dummy
        for v in res:
            cur.next = ListNode(v)
            cur = cur.next
        return dummy.next

a.t: O(n) - flattening, regrouping, and relinking are each linear

a.i: Hold group_prev, the node preceding the current group. Scan at most the nominal size ahead to learn how many nodes the group really holds; if even, perform count-1 head-insertions after group_prev, which reverses the chunk in place and parks the old head at the group tail - the resume anchor.
s: Initialize group_prev as the sentinel before head and nominal size = 1.
March ahead up to size nodes to measure the true group length.
If the count is even, repeatedly splice the node after the working head to the front of the group, count-1 times.
Advance group_prev to the processed group tail (the old head when reversed), bump the size, and continue while nodes remain.
a.t: O(n) - every node is scanned once and relocated at most once

w: Ship the array version unless constant space is explicitly demanded - it is nearly impossible to get wrong. Pitfalls: judging the final short group by nominal rather than real length, and losing your place after a reversal (old head becomes new tail and the next group_prev). Dry-run lists of lengths 1 through 10 to shake off off-by-one bugs. Follow-ups: reverse odd-length groups instead, honor an arbitrary size sequence, or reverse every group regardless of parity.
